name: Sonoran Loop — January
subtitle: Death Valley · Lake Havasu · Scottsdale · Superstitions · Saguaro · Tucson
summary: The warmest of the loops, and the one that charges you the most driving for it. Death Valley first, then straight down the Colorado River into Arizona and on into the Sonoran Desert — saguaro country, which begins around Wickenburg and exists on neither of the other routes. Phoenix and Tucson both sit around 20°C in January. Getting back to Las Vegas from Tucson is a 288-mile day, and that is the honest argument against this trip.
startEnd: Las Vegas, NV (Harry Reid International — LAS)

mustSee.name: Zabriskie Point
mustSee.why: Golden badlands at sunset, ten minutes from where you sleep. The best view in Death Valley for the least effort.

mustSee.name: Badwater Basin
mustSee.why: The lowest point in North America, 282 ft below sea level, at 18°C in January. Walk out onto the salt flats.

mustSee.name: Mesquite Flat Dunes
mustSee.why: Go at sunrise. Dunes the kids can run down, before the wind picks up and the light goes flat.

mustSee.name: Hoover Dam
mustSee.why: Park and walk out onto the bridge. Twenty minutes, no ticket, and it is still astonishing.

mustSee.name: London Bridge
mustSee.why: The actual bridge from the Thames, shipped here in 1968 and rebuilt block by numbered block. Nothing about it makes sense and that is the point.

mustSee.name: Desert Botanical Garden
mustSee.why: The one thing to pay for in Phoenix. Everything you have been driving past for a week, named and explained, on flat paths.

mustSee.name: The Superstition Mountains
mustSee.why: A wall of rock straight out of the back of Apache Junction, best in the last hour of light.

mustSee.name: Cactus Forest Loop Drive
mustSee.why: Eight paved miles through the thickest saguaro stand in the park. Doable without leaving the vehicle on the day the legs give out.

mustSee.name: Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum
mustSee.why: Routinely called one of the best museums in the country, and it is mostly outdoors. If you do one paid thing on this trip, do this.

mustSee.name: Mission San Xavier del Bac
mustSee.why: White as bone against the desert and in continuous use since 1797. Ten miles south of Tucson and free to walk into.

watchOuts.title: Book the Phoenix nights before anything else
watchOuts.text: Book the Phoenix-area nights first, then Tucson, then Lake Havasu. January to March is snowbird season across the whole Valley of the Sun — RV parks around Phoenix, Mesa and Apache Junction fill up months ahead and charge their annual peak, and hotel rooms follow. Death Valley and Wickenburg have far more slack.

watchOuts.title: Day 13 is 288 miles and it is not optional
watchOuts.text: Day 13 is 288 miles and the better part of six hours. Start early, fill up in Wickenburg, and plan nothing else that day. It is the price of reaching Tucson from Las Vegas and back inside two weeks — the same arithmetic that kept Saguaro off the Southwest Loop.

watchOuts.title: It is warm, not hot
watchOuts.text: No night on this route is expected to freeze. Tucson is the highest place you sleep at 2,430 feet, where January lows average about 4°C, and Wickenburg can touch freezing for an hour or two before dawn on a cold snap. Phoenix and Lake Havasu stay around 7°C at night and 20°C by day. Nothing here needs winterising.

watchOuts.title: The Apache Trail is only paved to Tortilla Flat
watchOuts.text: The Apache Trail is paved as far as Tortilla Flat and that is the section to drive — Canyon Lake and the saloon. Beyond it the road turns to dirt and long stretches have been closed since the 2019 fire and the floods that followed. Check the state's road status before you set out, and do not plan to drive through to Roosevelt Lake.

watchOuts.title: Death Valley is still closing roads
watchOuts.text: Flood damage persists. Bonnie Clare Road and Scotty's Castle are closed with no reopening date, North Highway has loose gravel and missing shoulders, southern Badwater Road has soft shoulders and unpaved sections, and Emigrant Campground is closed indefinitely. Check the park's conditions page a week before departure.

watchOuts.title: The park pass does not cover the good bits in the middle
watchOuts.text: The America the Beautiful pass covers Death Valley and both halves of Saguaro. It does not cover Lost Dutchman or Lake Havasu, which are state parks, and it does nothing at all for the Desert Botanical Garden, the Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum or Taliesin West — the three best things in the middle of this trip, all of which charge per person.

watchOuts.title: Long empty stretches — fill up early
watchOuts.text: US-93 and the Colorado River road both have long empty stretches. Top off in Kingman on the way down, in Wickenburg before day 13, and before entering Death Valley, where in-park fuel at Furnace Creek is notably expensive.

watchOuts.title: Price the unlimited-miles package
watchOuts.text: If the rental charges per mile at around $0.35, 1,545 miles adds roughly $540. On this route more than the others, always price the unlimited-miles package.

pros: The warmest of the three loops. Phoenix and Tucson both average around 20°C in January, and no night is expected to freeze.
Saguaro cactus country. The giant saguaro grows only in the Sonoran Desert and appears on neither of the other routes.
Two national parks, two state parks, and the Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum, which is worth the drive on its own.
Cities, for once. Phoenix and Tucson mean real supermarkets, real restaurants and a hospital — which matters with six people for two weeks.
Day 9 is 28 miles. Half the trip is genuinely easy driving on main highways.
One set of flights, one vehicle, one loop. Nothing is one-way.
cons: Day 13 is 288 miles and the better part of six hours. There is no way to avoid it — Tucson is simply a long way from Las Vegas.
Day 7 is another 210 miles. Two of the fifteen days carry most of the driving on the whole trip.
1,545 miles in total, 180 more than the Low Desert Loop, and much of that is main highway rather than scenery.
January is peak snowbird season across Phoenix and Tucson. RV parks book out months ahead and rooms are at their annual high.
The middle of the trip is a metropolitan area of five million people. If the point of the holiday is empty desert, this is the wrong loop.
Death Valley still has flood damage: Scotty’s Castle and Bonnie Clare Road are closed indefinitely, and several roads have soft shoulders and unpaved sections.

notConsidered.reason: 6,800 feet, snow on the rim and nights around −8°C. It belongs to the Southwest Loop, where the cold is the whole bargain.
Warm, and on the far side of the Colorado. Putting them with Saguaro means two 280-mile days instead of one. That trip is the Low Desert Loop.
4,300 feet, and January nights there run below freezing. It also sits 120 miles off this loop in the wrong direction.
The warmest national monument in the country and genuinely worth seeing, but it is 140 miles south of Tucson on the Mexican border and costs a whole day each way.
Both good, both about 90 miles past Tucson, and this trip already contains a 288-mile day.
Fifty miles southeast of Tucson, and tour tickets sell out weeks ahead. Worth it if you plan early — easy to miss if you do not.
Trailer rentals do not include a tow vehicle, and the major rental companies prohibit towing outright. Turo treats towing as a prohibited use that voids damage protection.

moneySavers.item: Sleep in Mesa or Apache Junction, not Scottsdale
moneySavers.detail: Scottsdale in January is the most expensive lodging on any of these routes. Mesa and Apache Junction are twenty-five minutes away, have the bulk of the region's RV parks, and put you closer to the Superstitions anyway. This is the single biggest lever in the budget.
Hole in the Rock is a ten-minute walk to a view over Phoenix, free, with parking at the bottom. Camelback is a chained scramble with a car park that fills by eight in the morning.

moneySavers.item: Skip Taliesin West unless somebody cares
moneySavers.detail: Tours start around $49 a head and run ninety minutes. Superb if anyone in the party is interested in Frank Lloyd Wright, an expensive hour if not.
Buy bedding and kitchen gear at a Las Vegas store on day one for $200-300 and leave it behind. Cheaper than per-person kit fees for six.

moneySavers.item: Buy the Desert Museum and Garden tickets online
moneySavers.detail: Both discount advance tickets against the gate price, and both sell timed entry that can run out on a January weekend. This is the one pair of tickets worth booking ahead.
Covers Death Valley and both districts of Saguaro. It does NOT cover Lost Dutchman or Lake Havasu, which are state parks, nor any of the museums and gardens.

options.name: Motorhome
options.tagline: Cheapest, warmest nights, and the hardest thing to book
options.summary: Transport and lodging in one vehicle, so you cook instead of eating out and there is nothing to book at six separate stops — except that on this route the one stop you do have to book, months ahead, is the Phoenix one, and it is the hardest booking on any of these trips.

vehicle.detail: Cruise America C30 · sleeps 7 · 7 seatbelts · 30 ft long, 8.33 ft wide, 12.2 ft high
vehicle.notes: Book by seatbelt count, not sleeping capacity. On this route the length limits that bite are Death Valley's 25 ft on Artist's Drive and Dante's View, and Gates Pass in Tucson, which is closed to RVs outright. The real constraint is not the vehicle, it is finding a Phoenix-area site in January.

Two thirds of the route is main highway, which is the easy kind of driving in a 30-footer

2.label: Not in the motorhome:
2.text: Artist's Drive is closed to vehicles over 25 ft. Take the separate rental car — it is in the budget for exactly this.

3.label: Not in the motorhome:
3.text: The final climb to Dante's View has the same 25 ft limit. Rental car again.

7.label: Book this stop first.
7.text: January to March is snowbird season across the Valley of the Sun. The full-hookup parks around Phoenix, Mesa and Apache Junction are booked months ahead and priced at their annual peak. Nothing else on this trip is anywhere near as hard to get.

9.label: Not in the motorhome:
9.text: The Apache Trail past Canyon Lake. Even the paved section is narrow with tight curves and is no place for a 30-footer, and beyond Tortilla Flat it is dirt and partly closed. Do Lost Dutchman and the Canyon Lake vista and turn around.

11.label: Not in the motorhome:
11.text: Gates Pass is posted closed to RVs — a narrow switchback climb with no shoulders. Saguaro West and the Desert Museum are still open to you the long way round on Ajo Way, which adds about twenty minutes. You lose the sunset, not the park.

14.label: The motorhome goes back today.
14.text: Allow half a day for the return process, then a hotel for the last night — the flight morning stays simple.

options.name: Car and lodging
options.tagline: More expensive, and it makes the two long days bearable
options.summary: A seven-seater and a room every night. It costs meaningfully more, and almost all of the gap is food and lodging — but this is the route with a 288-mile day and a 210-mile day in it, and that is worth more here than on either of the others.

vehicle.detail: Chrysler Pacifica · Honda Odyssey · Chevrolet Suburban · 7 seats
vehicle.notes: A minivan is better for people, a Suburban better for luggage. Fourteen days from Las Vegas including airport concession fees. On a route with a 288-mile day and a 210-mile day, the comfort of the vehicle matters more here than on either of the others.

days.notes: Pick up the vehicle and drive straight in. Furnace Creek sits 190 feet below sea level — January highs around 18°C, lows around 4°C.

days.headline: Out of the valley to the dam
days.notes: Back through Las Vegas and out the far side. Boulder City was built in 1931 to house the men constructing Hoover Dam, and is still the only town in Nevada where gambling is illegal. The dam is ten minutes away and Lake Mead is closer than that.

pois.name: Hoover Dam
pois.caption: Park and walk out onto the bridge — 20 minutes, no ticket needed.

photos.caption: Park and walk out onto the bridge — 20 minutes, no ticket needed.

pois.name: Lake Mead
pois.caption: Hemenway Harbor, ten minutes from Boulder City and the bighorn sheep come down to the grass.

days.headline: Down US-93 to the river
days.notes: Through Kingman, where Route 66 crosses the highway, and on down to the Colorado. Lake Havasu City was founded in 1963 by a chainsaw manufacturer, who then bought London Bridge to give people a reason to come.

pois.name: Kingman
pois.caption: Where Route 66 crosses US-93. The Powerhouse museum and the old depot.

photos.caption: Where Route 66 crosses US-93. The Powerhouse museum and the old depot.

pois.name: London Bridge
pois.caption: The 1831 Thames bridge, bought in 1968 and rebuilt here block by numbered block.

photos.caption: The 1831 Thames bridge, bought in 1968 and rebuilt here block by numbered block.

days.headline: A day on the water
days.notes: Lake Havasu runs to around 18°C in January — warm enough to be out on a boat, too cold to swim. London Bridge is the actual bridge that stood over the Thames from 1831: bought from the City of London in 1968, taken apart, and rebuilt here block by numbered block.
activities: Boat or kayak on the lake

pois.name: Lake Havasu State Park
pois.caption: Around 18°C in January — warm enough for a boat, too cold to swim.

photos.caption: Around 18°C in January — warm enough for a boat, too cold to swim.

days.headline: Into saguaro country
days.notes: The long transfer day, and the one where the desert changes under you. Somewhere south of Parker the first saguaros appear — they grow nowhere on earth but the Sonoran Desert, and nowhere at all on the other two routes. By the time you reach Phoenix they are everywhere.
activities: The drive down through Parker and Wickenburg

pois.name: Saguaro country
pois.caption: Somewhere around Wickenburg the first giant saguaros appear. They grow nowhere else on earth.

photos.caption: Somewhere around Wickenburg the first giant saguaros appear. They grow nowhere else on earth.

days.headline: Phoenix in shirtsleeves
days.notes: 18 to 21°C and dry. The Desert Botanical Garden is the best introduction to this desert there is, and being a garden it suits everybody in the party. Camelback is a hard scramble with chains and drop-offs; Papago Park next door gives you a ten-minute walk to the same kind of view.
activities: Hole in the Rock, Papago Park

days.headline: Under the Superstitions
days.notes: Twenty-eight miles, the shortest day on any of these routes. Lost Dutchman State Park sits directly beneath the Superstition Mountains, and the Apache Trail climbs behind them to Canyon Lake and Tortilla Flat, a town with six residents and one saloon.

days.headline: The east half of Saguaro
days.notes: Saguaro National Park is two separate districts on opposite sides of Tucson. The east one — Rincon Mountain — has the Cactus Forest Loop Drive: eight paved miles through the densest stand of saguaro in the park, and you can do the whole thing without leaving the vehicle if legs have run out.

days.headline: The west half, and the best museum in the desert
days.notes: The Arizona-Sonora Desert Museum is a zoo, a botanical garden and a natural history museum on one site, and is routinely called one of the best museums in the country. It is next door to the western half of Saguaro. Mission San Xavier del Bac, ten miles south, has been in continuous use since 1797.

days.headline: North, and the long way home begins
days.notes: Back up through Phoenix and out the far side to Wickenburg, an 1863 gold town that runs on horses now. Vulture City, twelve miles south, is the mine that started it — abandoned in 1942 and left standing. This is the first and easier half of the drive home.

days.headline: 288 miles up the river
days.notes: The longest day on any of these routes, and there is no version of this trip without it. West to Parker, then north along the Colorado through Lake Havasu and Needles and up US-95 into Nevada. It is a good drive and it is still the better part of six hours.

pois.name: Parker Dam
pois.caption: The deepest dam in the world — two thirds of it is below the riverbed.

photos.caption: The deepest dam in the world — two thirds of it is below the riverbed.

days.headline: A last day in Las Vegas
days.notes: A free day before the Saturday flight home, and a spare one if weather cost you a day earlier in the trip. After yesterday's 288 miles, nobody will want to drive anywhere.

days.headline: Fly home
days.notes: The Saturday flight home. Anything still rented goes back at the airport on the way in.
